problem.problem:
Erin is smart. Fiona is quiet. Gary is blue. Gary is kind. Gary is quiet. Gary is red. Harry is smart. If Harry is smart then Harry is kind. Quiet, smart things are blue. If something is green and smart then it is not blue. Kind things are quiet. All blue, green things are smart. Red things are furry. If Harry is smart and Harry is blue then Harry is red.

Determine whether the following statement is true, false, or unknown:
Harry is furry.
raw_logic_programs:
Predicates:
Smart($x, bool) ::: Is x smart?
Quiet($x, bool) ::: Is x quiet?
Blue($x, bool) ::: Is x blue?
Green($x, bool) ::: Is x green?
Red($x, bool) ::: Is x red?
Kind($x, bool) ::: Is x kind?
Furry($x, bool) ::: Is x furry?

Facts:
Smart(Erin, True) ::: Erin is smart.
Quiet(Fiona, True) ::: Fiona is quiet.
Blue(Gary, True) ::: Gary is blue.
Kind(Gary, True) ::: Gary is kind.
Quiet(Gary, True) ::: Gary is quiet.
Red(Gary, True) ::: Gary is red.
Smart(Harry, True) ::: Harry is smart.

Rules:
Smart(Harry, True) >>> Kind(Harry, True) ::: If Harry is smart then Harry is kind.
Quiet($x, True) && Smart($x, True) >>> Blue($x, True) ::: Quiet, smart things are blue.
Green($x, True) && Smart($x, True) >>> Blue($x, False) ::: If something is green and smart then it is not blue.
Kind($x, True) >>> Quiet($x, True) ::: Kind things are quiet.
Blue($x, True) && Green($x, True) >>> Smart($x, True) ::: All blue, green things are smart.
Red($x, True) >>> Furry($x, True) ::: Red things are furry.
Smart(Harry, True) && Blue(Harry, True) >>> Red(Harry, True) ::: If Harry is smart and Harry is blue then Harry is red.

Query:
Furry(Harry, True) ::: Harry is furry.
